chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Walid and al-Abbas ibn Amir from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who breastfed me and also breastfed a boy with me, and for that boy there is a brother from his father and mother; is it permissible for me to marry his daughter? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.أَخٌ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: A brother from his father and mother (full sibling)
key_terms.أَرْضَعَتْ صَبِيّاً مَعِي: She breastfed a boy with me
key_terms.فَيَحِلُّ لِي: Then it is permissible for me

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of a boy who was breastfed by the same woman who breastfed him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the nursing bond (radāʿ) is established through the direct act of a woman feeding an infant, meaning the daughter of the boy she nursed is not a mahram to the narrator. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between direct nursing relationships and collateral ties, ensuring that marriage prohibitions are not extended beyond the explicit textual evidence. It serves as a practical legal precedent for determining kinship networks in cases of shared wet-nursing.
